dialogue.content: I'll have 12 unused PTO days at the end of 2026. How many of them do I lose, and is there a deadline for using the ones I keep?

With 12 unused PTO days at the end of 2026, you'd **lose 2 days** and keep **10 days**.

- **Carryover limit:** 10 days (80 hours) per calendar year. This was raised from 5 days by the People Operations announcement of 2025-11-17, which explicitly replaces Section 5 of the PTO Policy (HR-101) and the matching handbook section. The announcement states it is the rule until the policy is reissued.
- **Forfeiture:** PTO above the 10-day limit is forfeited on December 31 — so 2 of your 12 days are forfeited at year-end (except where state law prohibits forfeiture).
- **Deadline for the days you keep:** carried-over PTO must be used by **June 30** of the following year (June 30, 2027 for your 2026 rollover). The old March 31 deadline no longer applies.

Note the older policy and handbook documents still show 5 days / March 31; those figures are superseded. If you're outside the US, the Netherlands addendum is unaffected by this change, so check with People Operations about which rules apply to you.
